bullets.title: FOXA-ROKU Acquisition: Fox Buys Roku for $22B ($160/sh); ROKU Downgraded Across Street
bullets.body: Fox Corp agreed to acquire Roku for $160/share ($96 cash + 0.9693 FOXA Class A shares), valuing the deal at ~$22B EV. Combined company becomes the 3rd-largest US TV player with ~10% viewership share and targets $400M cost synergies; deal expected to close H1 2027. ROKU downgraded to neutral/hold at 8+ analysts post-announcement (JPM, Wolfe, Piper Sandler, Evercore, Susquehanna, Citizens, William Blair, Loop Capital, Oppenheimer, KeyBanc); FOXA down ~16% on dilution and leverage concerns; pro forma net leverage ~2.8x.

bullets.title: ACN: Q3 Earnings Miss, FY26 Growth Cut to 3-4%; Morgan Stanley Downgrades to EW
bullets.body: Accenture Q3 revenue $18.72B slightly missed consensus; bookings -2% YoY to $19.3B, with Managed Services book-to-bill below 1x for first time since 2019. FY26 revenue growth guidance cut to 3-4% (from 3-5%); adj. EPS beat at $3.80. Announced $4.175B acquisition of Dragos, runZero, and NetRise in OT cybersecurity. Morgan Stanley downgraded to EW (PT $177 from $240); JPMorgan maintains OW (PT $179); UBS maintains Buy ($275 PT); William Blair downgraded to market perform; ACN stock down ~25% on the week.

bullets.title: MU: Citi Raises PT to $1,200; Earnings June 24 with $20.57 EPS Consensus; DRAM Prices +200%
bullets.body: Citi raises Micron PT to $1,200 (10x CY27E EPS), lifting FY26/27 EPS estimates by 4-10% on stronger-than-expected DRAM pricing; DRAM spot up 52% since January, 21% above contract. DRAM supply expected 5% undersupplied in 2026 with ASPs +200% full-year. MU reports June 24 AH with consensus EPS $20.57 and revenue $35.56B. JPM notes MU as next major catalyst after Fed.

bullets.title: WDC/STX: Morgan Stanley Raises PTs ($650/$1,035); HDD Pricing Targeting $25-30/TB vs <$15 Today
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley raised WDC PT to $650 and STX to $1,035 after Asia supply chain checks confirm HDD cycle elongation through CY28 minimum. Demand growing 40-50% annually while supply grows only 30-35%; customers signing LTAs through 2032. Base case FY28 EPS ~70% above Street consensus. WDC up 32.6% for the week, STX also surging.

bullets.title: INTC: +10% on Week on Trump-Announced AAPL Chip Partnership; 18A-P Now in Risk Production
bullets.body: President Trump announced Apple agreed to work with Intel to design and build chips in the US; deal estimated at ~$1-1.2B annually (~5% of TSMC's Apple business). Intel simultaneously began risk production of 18A-P chip node (9% better performance or 18% lower power vs 18A); 14A process achieving ~0.5 defect density. Intel up ~10% on the announcement, hitting 52-week highs.

bullets.title: AAPL: Unavoidable Price Hikes on Memory/Storage Costs; JPM Expects Modest ~$50 iPhone ASP Increase
bullets.body: Apple CEO Tim Cook confirmed product price increases are unavoidable as memory/storage costs surge (4x YoY at component level; 80-90% BOM inflation). JPM expects iPhone 18 ASP increases of ~$50 (mid-single-digit %), well below press estimates of $200+, citing $40 in component savings offsets and $15 from modem vertical integration. Apple also planning camera-equipped AirPods in 2027 and foldable iPhone for fall 2026 at ~$2,000+.

bullets.title: PLTR: Wolfe Resumes at Peer Perform; NRR 150%, Revenue +85% YoY, But Trades at 30x CY27 Revenue
bullets.body: Wolfe relaunched PLTR coverage at Peer Perform; acknowledges best-in-class AI software execution with NRR 150%, revenue +85% YoY (accelerating), backlog +97% YoY on 1K+ customers. FY26-29 revenue CAGR estimated at 39-55%. Stock at 30x CY27 revenue and 65x EPS (~2x software peers), fair value $100-190; UBS separately maintains Buy at $200 PT.

bullets.title: CRM: Acquires Fin for $3.6B to Expand Agentforce; Organic cRPO Decelerated to 8.5%
bullets.body: Salesforce acquired AI customer service platform Fin for ~$3.6B all-cash (~9x trailing ARR); Fin has $400M ARR growing 37% (AI Agent product $100M+ ARR growing 350% YoY). Deal closes FY4Q27 with no guidance change. Separately, KeyBanc flagged organic cRPO growth decelerated 250bps YoY to 8.5% and organic current bookings declined 1.9%; CRM down 13 consecutive days heading into the week.

bullets.title: MSFT: Considering DeepSeek for Copilot Cowork; Microsoft Sells AI Models to Chinese Companies Including ByteDance ($1B+ Annually)
bullets.body: Microsoft is considering offering DeepSeek as a cheaper hosted alternative for Copilot Cowork and is also evaluating usage-based pricing. Bloomberg reported ByteDance is on track to spend $1B+ annually on Microsoft AI/cloud services; Ant Group, Meituan, and Tencent also spend significantly via Azure. OpenAI has complained privately about insufficient safeguards. Separately, MSFT's $3B Oracle cloud lease fell through on security/compliance concerns.

bullets.title: HOOD: Up 16% on Week; SEC Tokenized-Stock Exemption Proposal; 10% Workforce Reduction
bullets.body: Robinhood surged 16.1% WoW after SEC proposed allowing tokenized stocks under an innovation exemption. Separately, Robinhood announced a ~10% workforce reduction (~290 roles) citing high-performance culture maintenance; restructuring charges estimated at ~$28M. AFRM also up 11.7% on improved credit card master trust data.

bullets.title: AMZN: In Talks to Sell Custom AI Chips to Other Companies; AWS Summit Highlights Agentic AI
bullets.body: Amazon is in discussions to sell custom AI chips to other companies for data center use, directly challenging Nvidia. Citi projects AWS revenue growth to accelerate to +37% YoY in FY27 on agentic AI scaling; AWS Bedrock AgentCore agent task volume up 15x in six months. Amazon also facing potential FTC lawsuit over advertiser misrepresentation with possible billions in civil penalties.

bullets.title: GEV: +18% on Week; FERC Data Center Interconnection Approval Bullish for IPPs (TLN, VST, CEG)
bullets.body: GE Vernova surged 18% WoW on AI capex tailwinds. FERC unanimously approved Trump's plan to accelerate AI data center grid connections, directing grids to connect large loads in 'timely and orderly manner'; PUCT approved Batch 0 interconnection process covering 35 GW baseload and 65 GW under study. Goldman Sachs initiated TLN at Buy ($499 12-month PT); Bernstein initiated CEG at Outperform ($296 PT), VST at Outperform ($181 PT).

bullets.title: SNAP: SPECS AR Glasses Launch at $2,195; Analysts Cautious on Form Factor and Competition
bullets.body: Snap unveiled SPECS AR glasses with 51-degree FOV and 4-hour battery at $2,195 targeting developers and early adopters with ~100K units stretch goal for v1. Analysts broadly cautious—Citi maintains Neutral noting multiple generations needed for mass adoption. SNAP stock fell 6.5% on the announcement amid competition from META Ray-Ban glasses at $224-$799 and GOOGL-partnered WRBY/Gentle Monster options.

bullets.title: AVGO: JPM Double-Downs on Bull Case; TPU v9 2nm On-Track; $250-300B FY28 XPU Revenue Target
bullets.body: JPMorgan's Harlan Sur defended AVGO on Asia supply chain noise; TPU v8i 3nm 'Sunfish' fully qualified with 18+ month lead over Google's MediaTek alternative; Google/AVGO 5-year agreement through TPU v11 with commitments to increase revenues annually through 2031. AVGO targeting 2027 AI revenue growth of 2-2.5x with 2028 doubling again; XPU design win pipeline includes 6 frontier model builders plus Apple, Softbank, Sambanova.

bullets.title: ANET: vNDR Positive; PT Raised to $200; 1.6T Switch Architecture in 2H26
bullets.body: KeyBanc raised ANET PT to $200 from $178 following meetings; 1.6T switch (7060XE7) represents new rack-scale architecture shipping 4Q26/1Q27. XPU scaling from hyperscalers creates structural open-networking opportunity; revenue growth expected ~28% in CY26 and 25-30% in CY27. AI revenue target $3.5B in CY26.

bullets.title: RH: Q1 Beat but Q2 Guide Light; Estates Launch Is Key H2 Catalyst
bullets.body: RH beat Q1 EPS by $0.15 with gross margin 230bps above consensus, but Q2 revenue growth guidance (+0.5-2.5%) missed the +4.6% consensus. Management guides significant H2 uptick driven by $75M backlog tailwind and Estates sourcebook launch in Milan/London. Hedgeye flipped to long, citing end of heavy investment cycle and pivot to margin harvesting.

bullets.title: DKNG: NY/NJ/PA Sports Betting GGR Under Pressure from Knicks Championship and World Cup Parlays
bullets.body: NY OSB 2QTD GGR tracking -18% YoY with only +3% handle growth; DKNG market share fell to 33% from 35% in 2Q. NJ May sports betting GGR -17% YoY; DKNG NJ handle +12% but GGR -5% on collapsed hold. Fanatics is the only sportsbook with positive 2QTD GGR (+4% YoY), gaining 199bps of share. Negative holds driven by outsized betting volumes on Knicks championship and Team USA FIFA World Cup victory.

bullets.title: NFLX: Denies Lionsgate Interest; Expanding Traditional Broadcaster Partnerships; Radford Studio Acquisition
bullets.body: Netflix denied acquiring Lionsgate despite media reports and also clarified it did not bid for Roku. Netflix is acquiring Radford Studio Center for ~$400M (vs 2021 sale price of $1.85B after lenders repossessed). Netflix CEO confirmed strategy to add more traditional broadcasters to platform after TF1 deal in France; UK government also proposing to force YouTube and Meta to make UK news more prominent.

bullets.title: SHOP: Spring 2026 Editions Highlight AI Commerce Tools; UBS Neutral on Modest Near-Term Campaigns Upside
bullets.body: JPMorgan maintains Overweight on SHOP ($150 PT); Spring Editions showcased AI catalog converting 2x higher, Campaign Autopilot across FB/IG/ChatGPT/SNAP, AI Sales Associate in Inbox, and POS v11 cutting checkout time. UBS maintains Neutral; Shop Campaigns revenue doubled in 2025 with merchant adoption tripling, but near-term contribution modest (~low-MSD% of gross profit by 2028). Shopify rolling out AI tool for merchants to run campaigns and planning ads in ChatGPT and Microsoft.

bullets.title: DELL: Wins $1.44B US Air Force Contract; HPE Discover Confirms AI Infrastructure Demand
bullets.body: Dell Federal Systems awarded a $1.44B firm-fixed-price call order for US Air Force Microsoft enterprise license renewal. HPE at Discover 2026 confirmed robust AI server demand with supply-constrained backlog expected to remain elevated exiting FY26; networking approaching +10% FY26 growth with +8-12% FY27 guidance; Juniper/Aruba integration ahead of schedule. Citi maintains Buy on HPE.
